ledger.note: 21 May 1962: Indonesian forces hold ground. After the 'infiltration phase of Operation Trikora began' on 15 January 1962, 'Indonesian forces managed to take over on 21 May 1962' at Teminabuan 'and fly the Indonesian flag on the compound'; 'A successful paratrooper operation occurred on 24 June 1962, with the target Merauke'. Sukarno had decreed the People's Triple Command on 19 December 1961.

ledger.note: 15 August 1962: the New York Agreement. 'the Netherlands signed the New York Agreement with Indonesia on 15 August 1962'; the page gives no ceasefire date ('arranged a Dutch-Indonesian ceasefire').

October 1962: the United Nations takes over the administration. 'the territory was placed under the United Nations Temporary Executive Authority in October 1962' (infobox disestablished: 1 October 1962); sovereignty passed to Indonesia only on 1 May 1963, so the dossier runs to that date as the sibling republic-of-indonesia dossier expects. The event is a status caption, not a new name.

wars.outcome: No Dutch defeat in the field: Indonesian infiltration from 15 January 1962 (Battle of Arafura Sea), Teminabuan taken on 21 May and Merauke attacked by paratroopers on 24 June, the planned Biak assault called off; the Netherlands signed the New York Agreement on 15 August 1962 and the territory passed to the UN and then to Indonesia.
wars.note: The Dutch New Guinea page says Sukarno issued the Tri Komando Rakjat on 19 December 1961 and that the New Guinea Council took office on 5 April 1961 and adopted the Morning Star flag on 1 December 1961.

certainty.note: The eastern frontier is the 141st meridian ('The Dutch established the 141st meridian as the eastern frontier'); the interior was unadministered and the coast posts few, so the western and interior limits are soft but there are no neighbours there.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch (counterpart named by the dutch-east-indies, republic-of-indonesia and se-04-a ledgers). Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the end: the Dutch New Guinea infobox gives 1 October 1962 as disestablishment (UNTEA); the republic-of-indonesia dossier gains the land on 1 May 1963 from this dossier's slug, so the dossier runs to May 1963 and 1962-10 is a status caption (UNTEA, a United Nations Temporary Executive Authority with no dossier: suggest slug united-nations-temporary-executive-authority); (2) the Operation Trikora page does not confirm that the handover to UNTEA took place on 1 October 1962; (3) the Indonesian sibling dates its contest from 24 June 1962 (Merauke), here from 21 May 1962 (Teminabuan, the first ground the page has Indonesia holding): the reviewer should pick one; (4) Teminabuan's coordinates are the researcher's; (5) the page gives no Dutch events before 1949 (the 1848 claim 'rests on the Sultanate of Ternate's claim', the 1898 posts at Fakfak and Manokwari are in the dutch-east-indies dossier); (6) the status change of 1954 (colony to overseas territory), the New Guinea Council (5 April 1961) and the Morning Star flag (1 December 1961) are constitutional and not events here; (7) Indonesia's 1969 Act of Free Choice is for the Indonesian dossier.
